inputCoverage.agencyScope: Complete features intersecting input window from existing source cache; not a fresh agency census

recommendation.summary: Review a segment-level merge: keep one overlapping alignment and verify the outlying sections as possible unique ends or branches. Do not connect them automatically.
reasons: OpenStreetMap: 23% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 28% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 531.5 m.
NPS: 93% of its geometry lies within 15 m of the other source; 100% within 50 m. Median nearest-line offset 2.0 m.

Within the same input window, OpenStreetMap: 9,122 m long, median vertex spacing 12.8 m, 6,518 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor; NPS: 2,229 m long, median vertex spacing 17.3 m, 0 m outside the other source’s 50 m corridor.

Endpoint check: OpenStreetMap has 68 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment; NPS has 0 non-seam endpoint candidates over 75 m from the other alignment. These can be real additions, branches, or source gaps; inspect their connections.

DEM sanity check in the shared corridor: OpenStreetMap: 90th-percentile absolute terrain grade 3.2% over 44 sampled 50 m sections; NPS: 90th-percentile absolute terrain grade 3.2% over 39 sampled 50 m sections. Lower grade alone does not mean a route is more accurate.
Vertex density measures representation detail, not survey accuracy. Sharp turns may be genuine switchbacks; geometry alone cannot diagnose GPS multipath.
recommendation.limitations: Heuristic guidance, not an independent ground-truth verdict. Uses source geometry and frozen DEM only; no imagery interpretation or route editing. DEM measures ground surface, not surveyed trail elevation. Full agency inputs and OSM tile fragments have different lineage; no automatic edits.
